Complete layouts for address space, memory area, folio, page and page table entry structures.
Global lock ordering among address space, area, table and folio locks beyond observed pairing.
Behavior of file hooks for fault, surrounding population, page write preparation and frame write preparation.

findings.text: A globally visible helper clears the entry at a supplied address and invalidates the corresponding translation cache only when the prior entry was accessible. It returns the prior entry so callers can continue with reclamation or reuse decisions.

A globally visible helper publishes newly allocated anonymous folio mappings with area derived protections and youth tracking, establishing reverse mapping and reclamation membership as part of becoming visible and maintaining translation cache coherence.

Missing entry dispatch separates anonymous areas from file backed areas. File dispatch distinguishes absent file support with a locked recheck that separates transient clearing from genuine absence, read handling with an initial surrounding population attempt followed by permission validation and delegation to file support with table preallocation performed before folio acquisition, and write handling split between private copy and shared coordination. Read completion proceeds through finalization with careful folio lock and reference lifetime management, and any unused preallocated table is released.

Anonymous missing handling rejects shared anonymous configurations, ensures middle level presence, serves reads from a shared zero backing unless forbidden by the address space, and allocates private folios for writes including possible multi page extents aligned to folio size. Under table lock it verifies that no concurrent population occurred and that multi page ranges remain empty, checks address space stability and user fault interception, then publishes the mapping. Shortages and transient mapping failures follow distinct memory exhaustion and silent retry paths with proper release.

Preallocation chooses a zeroed movable folio when zeroing is requested and a plain movable folio otherwise, then applies group charging with release on failure and applies swap rate throttling before returning. Large anonymous selection is skipped when user fault monitoring is armed, filters allowable orders by area suitability and containment, requires fully empty aligned ranges with preference for the highest feasible order, validates charging and deferred accounting, and falls back to single page preallocation when no large order remains.

Shared write handling separates raw frame mappings from page backed mappings. The raw frame path optionally invokes a frame write preparation hook after releasing the table lock and confirming hook permission, then completes through common finalization that reacquires and revalidates. The page backed path holds an extra reference across hook invocation with similar lock release and validation, finalizes, then performs dirty marking with time and writeback coordination. When no hook is present the current mapping is reused directly without hook dispatch.

Small anonymous reuse requires absence of merging markers, a reference count consistent with sole mapping plus optional reclamation or swap cache presence, draining of remote caches, successful nonblocking exclusive acquisition, release of swap cache membership, and final confirmation of sole ownership before transferring the folio to the faulting area. Large anonymous reuse requires multiple mapped pages, absence of cross address space sharing indication observed as FOLIO_MM_IDS_SHARED_BITNUM and absence of merging, equality of mapped count and reference count stabilized under a dedicated large mapcount guard, and sanity bounds on extent and ownership. An alternate build configuration for large reuse is defined only as a build time failure.

Leaf table contents are examined and published only while holding the associated table lock obtained through a mapping operation, with explicit unmapping unlock on every exit. After any interval without the lock the handler reacquires and compares current contents against the saved original, refreshing translation caches when a race is detected and abandoning the stale path. Accessed emulation on architectures without hardware support and user copy retry after failure both follow the same revalidation discipline.

Folio exclusivity is obtained with blocking or opportunistic acquisition depending on context, held across dirty marking and ownership transfer, and released after capturing address space membership locally to survive later truncation. Writeback throttling may temporarily release the address space lock while pinning the file, reporting completion to the caller in that case. Area read protection is released with a retry indication before invoking file hooks when surrounding population support is absent and area locking was used.

The fault descriptor threaded through dispatch carries the faulting area observed as vma with address, middle level position observed as pmd with leaf position observed as pte plus lock observed as ptl, current and saved entries including original observed as orig_pte, reason flags observed as flags, an optional page result observed as page, and an optional preallocated table observed as prealloc_pte. Flags distinguish write intent and preparation, area lock holding and saved entry validity. The same descriptor is reused across permission checks and finalization, with the leaf slot cleared or revalidated around lock release.

Hardware poison observed during copy or after file hook invocation follows dedicated poison handling including unmapping and cache eviction, with a possible silent retry when a clean entry was dropped. Persistently unreadable user sources trigger a warning and zero fill. Shared anonymous faults, swap backed write preparation and genuinely absent entries without file support produce bus errors. Middle level allocation failure and folio exhaustion produce memory exhaustion indications, while races produce no page or retry style outcomes.

When no page structure exists for the source, the handler maps the destination locally, suppresses faults, and attempts an atomic copy from the aligned user address. Architectures without hardware youth tracking first mark access under lock. Failure triggers revalidation under lock with a second attempt, and persistent failure results in warning plus zero fill, followed by cache maintenance, local unmapping and fault re enablement.

Outcomes are communicated through symbolic names including VM_FAULT_OOM and VM_FAULT_SIGBUS for resource and access failures, VM_FAULT_NOPAGE and VM_FAULT_RETRY for revalidation paths, VM_FAULT_LOCKED and VM_FAULT_COMPLETED for ownership and lock release, VM_FAULT_HWPOISON and VM_FAULT_DONE_COW for special handling, with VM_FAULT_ERROR as a family marker tested to decide early return versus continuation.

Inputs use reason flags named FAULT_FLAG_WRITE and FAULT_FLAG_MKWRITE for write handling, FAULT_FLAG_VMA_LOCK for area lock holding, and FAULT_FLAG_ORIG_PTE_VALID for saved entry validity, together with area attributes named VM_SHARED and VM_WRITE plus anonymous checks and user fault write protection markers. Protection values for new mappings derive from area configuration, and zero backing selection respects address space policy.

Internal dispatch for missing entries and for file backed faults acts as the convergence point for anonymous allocation, surrounding population, hook invocation and shared coordination. Callers supply middle level context and descriptor state, while the dispatch paths own leaf lock management, stability checks, user fault interception and preallocation cleanup.

Anonymous publication updates address space anonymous residency in proportion to folio extent and records allocation statistics keyed by folio order, complementing table visibility and cache coherence maintenance performed during installation.
